topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
lecture_lines: Vectors are directed segments in 2D space.
Scaling and adding vectors build everything.
animations: Display and show v (#FF5733) and w (#33FF57).
Move vector v to end at (2,1) labeled 'v'.
Move vector w to end at (-1,2) labeled 'w'.
Animate v+w as a new arrow (#3357FF).
Flash both vectors v and w using color (#FFFFFF) on.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
lecture_lines: Span is the set of all reachable points.
Vectors A and B fill the 2D plane.
animations: Show scalar multiplication of v by 2 and w by -1.
Draw grid points illustrating combinations c1v + c2w.
Fill plane spanned by v and w with light blue (#00FFFF).
Move vector u across the spanned area to show reachability.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundant Vector
lecture_lines: Linear dependence: redundant vector adds no dimension.
Vector C lying on line A, B is redundant.
Redundant vectors provide no new navigation.
animations: Display vectors v (#FF5733) and w (#33FF57) over.
Add third vector u (#3357FF) on the plane.
Flash u in red (#FF0000) indicating dependence while displaying.

sections.title: The Concept of Basis
lecture_lines: Basis is the minimal spanning set.
Linearly independent vectors efficiently define space.
Basis is the most efficient coordinate system.
animations: Display standard basis vectors i-hat (#FF5733) and j-hat (#33FF57).
Scale i-hat by 3 and j-hat by 2 to reach (3,2).
Display grid lines defined by basis vectors.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
animations: Draw lines connecting these three concepts.
